root_cause_label: Agent solved a self-defined version of the task (custom example) rather than verifying against the actual benchmark test suite, submitting with a no-op command.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent built Cython extensions and fixed numpy compatibility issues for a custom test case, but never consulted or ran the actual grader test suite, culminating in a no-op submission at step 28 that leaves the real evaluation criteria unmet.
t_err_evidence: At step 7 the agent creates its own test script (/app/test_pyknotid.py) with a README example rather than examining the tests/ directory or the actual benchmark evaluation criteria; this locks the agent into solving a self-defined sub-problem for the rest of the trajectory.
t_commit_evidence: At step 28 the agent issues `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT` — a no-op — as its final action, providing no actual submission artifact and never running the benchmark test suite, making failure inevitable.
trigger_explanation: The agent never read the tests/ directory or the actual benchmark evaluation script. From step 7 onward it optimized for making a self-authored Python snippet succeed (e.g., computing an Alexander polynomial), which is not what the grader checks. The task requires the Cython extensions to be properly built and importable according to specific grader tests, but the agent substituted its own success criterion throughout.
forewarning_evidence: At step 15, pip attempted to upgrade numpy to 2.4.1 (violating the numpy==2.3.0 environment requirement) when re-installing pyknotid without --no-deps. The agent observed this in the truncated output but did not verify whether the upgrade completed or whether the numpy version constraint was still satisfied.
